subject: Velocity & pricing: per-token ladder — smoothing / marginal vs blended
messages:
From: Emily Park <emily@cureline.ai>
To: markus_klein@redwood-inference.com, procurement@cureline.ai
Cc: Cureline Diagnostics Procurement <procurements@cureline.ai>
Date: 2028-07-10T15:04:00-07:00
Subject: Velocity & pricing — initial usage profile and ask

Hi Markus,

Thanks for the demo last week — the team at Cureline is excited about Redwood's latency and the model catalog. We're pulling together procurement and want to validate pricing options for our hosted API usage. High level:

- Expected steady state: ~1.2B tokens/month within Q4 (text gen + embeddings mix)
- Ramp: pilot months (M1–M3) ~200–400M tokens, then step to steady state by M6
- Preference: usage-based per-token billing; open to commit tiers if it lowers unit cost

Two asks:
1) Can you share a clear worked example contrasting a pure marginal-breakpoint ladder vs a blended effective rate approach for our profile (especially for months M1–M6 with ramp)?
2) Would Redwood consider a short-term velocity lock (e.g., 3–6 months) where we guarantee a minimum average and receive a smoothing credit across the ramp?

I've attached our internal forecast and procurement guidance (Cureline_pricing_request_0708.pdf). Procurement will need clear invoice true-up language and a description of how breakpoints are smoothed for partial-month usage.

Can we do a 30-minute call on Tue/Thu next week to walk the numbers?

Best,
Emily Park
Head of Platform Partnerships
Cureline Diagnostics

--
Attachment: Cureline_pricing_request_0708.pdf (application/pdf)
From: markus_klein@redwood-inference.com
To: Emily Park <emily@cureline.ai>
Cc: monica_patel@redwood-inference.com, ben_carter@redwood-inference.com
Date: 2028-07-11T10:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Velocity & pricing — initial usage profile and ask

Hi Emily,

Thanks — received the forecast and appreciate the clarity on ramp. Short answers up front: yes, we can do both margin-style ladders and blended introductory structures, and yes, we can model a velocity lock. I've attached a worked pricing matrix (pricing_matrix_markus_v2.xlsx) that includes:

- Option A: Marginal ladder (breakpoints at 250M, 750M, 1.5B tokens) with marginal per-token rates and the math for month-by-month effective pricing.
- Option B: Blended intro (first 3 months at a single blended effective rate to simplify procurement) that flips into the marginal ladder thereafter.
- Option C: Velocity-lock addendum: committed effective rate for the committed months, with a true-up and cap on overage to protect both sides.

Notes on tradeoffs:
- Marginal ladders give the most accurate unit economics for Redwood (you only pay the marginal rate for the slice). That benefits heavy tail months.
- Blended intro simplifies forecasting and invoicing for procurement but can be slightly more expensive on units if your usage spikes unevenly.
- Velocity lock works best when you can commit a floor (e.g., 800M tokens/month average over 6 months); we can structure month-by-month true-ups so you don’t overpay during ramp months.

I recommend a hybrid: blended for the pilot (M1–M3) so procurement sees predictable invoices, then automatic switch to marginal ladder (Option A) from M4 onward, with a 6-month velocity-lock option we can add to the SOW if you want price protection.

Available Tue 8:30–11:30 or Thu 13:00–16:00 PT for a walk-through.

Cheers,
Markus Klein
Director, Strategic Sales
Redwood Inference

--
Attachment: pricing_matrix_markus_v2.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)
From: markus_klein@redwood-inference.com
To: monica_patel@redwood-inference.com, ben_carter@redwood-inference.com
Date: 2028-07-12T09:02:00-07:00
Subject: Internal: Cureline ask — margin floor and concessions

Monica / Ben,

Quick internal note before the call: Cureline's steady state is attractive but the ramp means we should protect unit economics. Proposal I'm going to present:

- Public list (baseline) rates unchanged
- Offer a 3-month blended intro at $0.0009/token equivalent (covers pilot) that flips to marginal ladder:
  - 0–250M: $0.00110/token
  - 250M–750M: $0.00085/token
  - 750M–1.5B: $0.00070/token
  - >1.5B: negotiate accelerator

- Velocity-lock option: if they sign commit for 6 months at an 800M average, we reduce the blended intro to $0.00082/token and include a monthly true-up; cap on credits to limit downside to ~$30k/month.

Ask: how far can we flex the floor? Finance prefers not to go below $0.00068 on marginal top-tier without legal sign-off. Also want marketing to avoid publicizing the velocity cap.

I'll frame it as a hybrid that reduces procurement friction. Thoughts?

-Markus
From: Emily Park <emily@cureline.ai>
To: markus_klein@redwood-inference.com
Cc: Cureline Diagnostics Procurement <procurements@cureline.ai>
Date: 2028-07-13T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Velocity & pricing — initial usage profile and ask

On Thu, Jul 11, 2028 at 10:22 AM, markus_klein@redwood-inference.com wrote:
> I recommend a hybrid: blended for the pilot (M1–M3) so procurement sees predictable invoices, then automatic switch to marginal ladder (Option A) from M4 onward, with a 6-month velocity-lock option we can add to the SOW if you want price protection.

Thanks — that framework makes sense. A few follow-ups from procurement:

1) Smooth breakpoints: procurement dislikes sudden cliffs in the month where they cross a breakpoint. Would Redwood consider a 15% smoothing corridor around each breakpoint (i.e., partial-volume weighted smoothing for months that cross)?
2) Blended intro: we prefer the blended rate to apply to tokens up to the blended-equivalent volume in the first 3 months (so they don't get penalized on a low pilot).
3) Velocity credits: if we commit to a 6-month average, how does the true-up flow on invoices? We prefer an end-of-term reconciliation vs monthly true-ups (one settlement ledger).

Also attach our procurement template — we need invoice language that gives us a single reconciliation at the end of the commitment period.

Would you be able to send a short term-sheet (1 page) that we can take to procurement that includes: blended intro price, marginal ladder, smoothing corridor definition, and the reconciliation approach?

Best,
Emily

--
Attachment: Cureline_procurement_template_0713.pdf (application/pdf)
From: markus_klein@redwood-inference.com
To: Emily Park <emily@cureline.ai>
Cc: monica_patel@redwood-inference.com, ben_carter@redwood-inference.com
Date: 2028-07-14T11:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Velocity & pricing — term-sheet and reconciliation approach

Hi Emily — thanks for the clear asks. Attached is a 1-page term-sheet and an offer PDF that implements your points. Highlights: 

- Blended intro: 3 months at $0.00088/token applied to actual tokens up to an aggregated blended-equivalent volume (we compute the blended cap based on your forecast).
- Marginal ladder thereafter (same breakpoints as in the matrix) with a 15% smoothing corridor applied to months that cross a breakpoint; smoothing is implemented as a weighted average across the slices for that month so there are no cliffs.
- Velocity-lock (optional addendum): 6-month commit at an 800M/month average. Reconciliation: we will do a single end-of-term true-up settlement (one invoice adjustment) rather than monthly reconciliations; that will be reflected in the SOW and invoice terms.

I've kept the concession envelope tight — top-tier marginal floor is $0.00070/token; if legal needs to build a clawback or accelerator we can add that. I also included an example math table in the PDF so procurement can see the numbers.

Next steps:
1) Review the attached redwood_offer_velocity_lock_v1.pdf with procurement.
2) If acceptable, I can push a DocuSign SOW (pre-filled, HubSpot deal CR-457) linking the velocity addendum.
3) Optional 30-min call to walk the term-sheet on Mon/Tue next week.

DocuSign: https://docusign.com/templates/REDWOOD-CR-457
HubSpot: https://hubspot.com/deal/CR-457

If procurement wants the single end-of-term true-up in the Master Services Agreement, loop legal and I will coordinate redlines.

Thanks — looking forward to closing this.

Best regards,
Markus Klein
Director, Strategic Sales
Redwood Inference
